forum.title: Has anyone successfully used the ST25R95 EMI FILTER CALCULATION.xlsm tool?
tags: ST25 NFC - RFID readers - ST25Rx00 series
forum.best_answer_content:
Hi Marco,

The antenna tuning of the ST25R95 is an iterative process. The input impedance of the antenna + matching network, seen from TX1/TX2, should be the complex conjugate of the equivalent source impedance of the ST25R95 plus EMI filter, so that at

13.56 MHz the reactive parts cancel and the resistive parts are matched for maximum power transfer.

According to AN5248, C2 mainly adjusts the tuning frequency, while C11/C12 mainly adjust the impedance magnitude. In practice, you should start from the Excel-calculated values, measure the input impedance with the board unpowered, and then fine-tune C2 first to center the resonance at 13.56 MHz, followed by C11/C12 to reach the desired impedance level. Since the components interact slightly, the tuning must be repeated until the target is reached.

After powering the board, also check the ST\_R0 voltage and keep it below the recommended limit. As noted in the application note, the target input impedance can be chosen above the ST25R95 output impedance, up to around 50 Ω if appropriate for the application.

For your latest example, it would mean to reduce C2 a little bit to move the 13.56MHz point to the real axe.

I expect that the whole resonance circle moves up:

![](https://uploads-eu-west-1.insided.com/stmicroelectronics-en/attachment/514e4a9a-75ae-44ac-85e4-438eab434c29.png)

BR Travis
forum.content_text:
Hello everyone,

Has anyone successfully used the **"ST25R95 EMI FILTER CALCULATION.xlsm"** spreadsheet?

I'm currently trying to use it for tuning the matching network of an ST25R95 design, but it doesn't seem to work correctly on my side. As soon as I modify any parameter or use the reset function, all the graphs disappear and I can no longer obtain any meaningful results.

At the moment, this tool would be very useful for optimizing the matching network, and without it I'm having some difficulties proceeding with the tuning process.

Has anyone experienced the same issue? Is there a specific Excel version, macro setting, or workaround required to make the spreadsheet work properly?

Any suggestions, advice, or alternative methods for tuning the matching network would be greatly appreciated.

Thank you in advance for your help.

Marco

Hello Marco,

 

I just downloaded the “ST25R95_EMI_FILTER_CALCULATION.xlsm” from https://www.st.com/en/embedded-software/stsw-st25r003.html .

 

When changing the antenna inductance from 1.2uH to 1.1uH and 2uH all matching values got updated and the graphs refreshed. For me the tool is working. Have you tried another PC / MS Office installation?

Did you perform any specific action?

BR Travis

scraped_replies.html:
Hi Travis,

I have tested the Excell sheet with a different version of MS office and it works correctly.
 

According to application note AN5248, without powering the board, I measured the circuit input impedance between TX1 and TX2 using a network analyzer. Please find a screenshot below.


My question is: how should I practically tune the values of C11, C12, and C2?

I understand that the tuning frequency can be adjusted using C2, while the impedance magnitude can be adjusted using C11 and C12. However, I do not fully understand the practical procedure for doing this.

The application note states that the matching network can be calculated by solving the impedance matching criterion:

Zin2 = Zout_EMI*

which allows the values of C11 = C12 and C2 to be determined.

However, I am struggling to understand how to apply this criterion in practice starting from the measured impedance.

Could you please provide some guidance on the tuning process?

Thank you for your help.

Best regards,
Marco
